BadAnswer.description: The broker gave an answer the web service cannot use.

Busy.description:
Too many history queries at once: eight wait for a turn already, or none
came within two seconds. Try again.

Conflict.description:
Another maintenance operation is in progress or may still be running,
the unit is busy with an operation of its own, or the request ID belongs
to another operation.

Internal.description:
Something failed inside the service; the journal names the cause under
the answer's `X-Request-Id`.

Invalid.description:
A parameter, a path segment or the body does not match the API, or a
history query cannot be answered as asked.

NotFound.description:
No recorded events for this ID, or no job of this ID that the user may
see.

Settling.description:
Too soon: the previous operation is settling, or this action is in its
cooldown.

SignInRequired.description: No valid session: sign in again.

TooLarge.description: The request body is larger than the service reads.

Unavailable.description:
Not available now, as the detail says: the user's rights cannot be
checked (Stalwart or the broker is away, or Garrison's setup is broken;
the session stays), what the route reads or runs is not there or took too
long, or the session could not be ended.

AttackNetwork.description: A network from which more than one address was seen.

AttackSource.description:
One address that failed to sign in, was banned or refused, or failed a
TLS handshake.

network.description: The /24 of an IPv4 address, the /64 of an IPv6 address.

refused.description:
Its connections that Stalwart refused while it blocked the address or
its network.

Connections Stalwart refused while it blocked their address; null
where the history holds none at all, as before `garrison stalwart
setup` asked Stalwart for them.

sources.description: Every address seen, also beyond the rows of the list.

unknownAccounts.description: Failed sign-ins that named no existing account.

AttackedAccount.description: An existing account that someone failed to sign in to.

Attacks.description:
Failed sign-ins, bans and TLS handshake errors of a stretch of the event
history. Each list has at most 50 rows, the busiest first; the bans are
the newest.

truncated.description: More events were recorded in the stretch than were read.

network.description:
The /64 of an IPv6 address, which Stalwart blocks with it unless an
account's count of failed sign-ins alone banned the address.

failingSince.description:
Since when the receiver runs without storing what Stalwart sends
(`receiver` is then "refusing"); null while it stores.

gapCount.description: Windows inside the history in which events may be missing.

lastBatchAge.description:
Seconds from `lastBatchAt` to this answer, by the server's clock; null
before the first batch. A page adds the time it waits since: the
browser's own clock may be another than the server's.

DeliveryCause.description: One cause of delays or bounces, without what differs between messages.

Destination.description: One domain mail was sent to and had a problem with.

cause.description: The cause named most often, shortened.

delays.description: Attempts that ended with a temporary failure.

delivered.description: Recipients a server of the domain accepted.

destinations.description: Domains with a delay or a bounce, also beyond the rows of the list.

Destinations.description:
Outgoing deliveries of a stretch of the event history by the domain they
went to and by the cause of their problems, and the messages that still
wait. Each list has at most 50 rows. Mail for this server's own mailboxes
is left out.

truncated.description: More events were recorded in the stretch than were read.

waiting.description: The messages that wait longest first.

ErrorDetail.description:
Every error answer of the API: a fixed text for people. For an internal
error the journal names the cause under the answer's `X-Request-Id`.

actor.description: The OIDC subject that asked for the job.

actorEmail.description: The subject's address when it asked; empty in older jobs.

other.description: Named links in the order the operator wrote them.

LogoutResponse.description:
The answer to a sign-out: the session is gone here. An error answers
otherwise, so `ok` is always true.

age.description:
Seconds from checkedAt to this answer, by the server's clock; null
when checkedAt cannot be read. A page that gets no newer answer adds
the time that passes and compares with maxAge.

stale.description: True when checkedAt is older than maxAge.

Period.description: The stretch a summary covers, up to now.

showSwitch.description:
The rows that switch between Garrison and the Stalwart WebUI, in
both menus; hidden until the user turns them on.

expiresAt.description: The second the session ends, since the epoch.

expiresIn.description:
Seconds from this answer to the session's end, by the server's clock.
A page counts them down on its own clock and then asks again: the
browser's clock may be another than the server's. Null where the end
lies further ahead than a session lasts, as for a row written while
the clock ran ahead: the page then counts nothing down.

SessionState.description:
The visitor's session, or `null` when nobody is signed in: the interface
asks before every sign-in, and that question is no error.

SwitchInfo.description: Whether the signed-in user wants the switch row in the Stalwart WebUI.

Trimmed.description:
The history begins later than its retention allows: events up to `until`
were removed to keep the size limit `limit` (`events` or `bytes`).

WaitingMessage.description: A queued message without a recorded end.

info.description: The web service: sign-in, the API and the compiled interface.
info.title: Garrison API

200.description: The actions the user may start, and the recent jobs.

get.summary: The maintenance actions the user may start, and recent jobs.

202.description: The broker took the job, which runs on its own; `replayed` says that the request ID was taken before and nothing new started.

post.summary: Start a maintenance action after its typed confirmation.

200.description: The job as the broker recorded it.

get.summary: One maintenance job and its result.

200.description: The failed sign-ins, bans and handshake errors of the period.

get.summary:
Failed sign-ins, Stalwart's bans and TLS handshake errors of the last day,
week or 30 days, by address, network and account.

200.description: What the event history covers, and whether the receiver runs.

get.summary: How complete the recorded event history is.

200.description: A page of deliveries and the cursor of the next older page.

get.summary: Queue lifecycles reconstructed from recorded events, newest first.

200.description: The message's summary and its recorded events.

get.summary: Every recorded event of one queued message.

200.description: The deliveries of the period by destination and cause, and the messages that wait.

get.summary:
Outgoing deliveries of the last day, week or 30 days by destination and
by the cause of their delays and bounces, and the messages that wait.

200.description: A page of events and the cursor of the next older page.
The session has ended here, and the answer removes its cookie.

post.summary: Sign out: end the session and revoke its access token.

200.description: The metric history of the period.

get.summary: Recorded metric history for the dashboard charts.

200.description: The preferences as they were saved.

put.summary: Save the signed-in user's theme and hidden modules.

200.description: The signed-in user, or `session: null` without a valid session.

get.summary:
The signed-in user: modules, actions, preferences and links; `null`
without a valid session.

200.description: A page of SMTP sessions and the cursor of the next older page.

get.summary: SMTP sessions reconstructed from recorded events, newest first.

200.description: The session's summary and its recorded events.

get.summary: Every recorded event of one SMTP session.

200.description: The latest snapshot with the observations of the user's modules; `available` is false before the first collection run.

get.summary: The latest status snapshot, limited to the user's modules.

200.description: Whether the signed-in user turned the switch rows on; `false` without a session.

get.summary:
Whether the signed-in user wants the switch rows. The "Switch to Garrison
WebUI" script asks from the Stalwart WebUI's origin, so this answer, and no
other, may be read there with the user's cookie. The rows are off until a
user turns them on, so without a session they stay hidden.
